What is the measure of $∠S$ above?
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that $△PQR$ is an equilateral triangle. Consequently, all of the interior angles must be equal to ${60}^{∘}:$ 

$$
m∠P=m∠PQR=m∠QRP={60}^{∘}
$$

Also, since $△QRS$ is an isosceles triangle, the base angles must have equal measure:

$$
m∠RQS=m∠S
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191212/assets/792155c685456f6c278fff5a0341f67358a8b0983d696cf55a6867c9c71ec7cb.png)

Notice also that $∠QRP$, $∠SRQ$ and $∠TRS$ are supplementary, therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠QRP+m∠SRQ+m∠TRS & ={180}^{∘} \\ {60}^{∘}+m∠SRQ+{70}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠SRQ+{130}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠SRQ & ={50}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, in $△QRS$, using the fact that the interior angles of a triangle sum to ${180}^{∘}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠RQS+m∠S+m∠SRQ & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠S+m∠S+{50}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ 2m∠S & ={130}^{∘} \\ m∠S & ={65}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$
